I’ll read the note and nearby progress records, then summarize what is established, what remains unresolved, and which next steps look most useful.

The latest work gives a sharper way to bound approximation errors and certifies several local windows without collisions. The main gap remains a uniform signed estimate for the actual heat coefficients. I’m checking how the new tests connect to that gap and what the local certificates demonstrate.

I verified that the 38 files match the latest review snapshot and replayed the Schur and dual-payment checkers; both reproduce their retained results. The coverage now includes four disconnected windows with 50 simple zero branches. Their derivative tests already exclude collisions, so the best next experiment is to test the sharper error bounds where those derivative margins are small.

The investigation has reached **sharp error bounds and rigorous local collision exclusions**, but the central arithmetic step remains open. Note 19 improves the tools for proving that step; it does not yet establish a uniform exclusion or a new global Newman bound.

The intended route is clear: a positive Newman threshold would produce a finite multiple real zero at a time when all zeros are real. At such a collision, the genuine derivatives must satisfy
\[
2q_3^2-3q_2q_4-\gamma q_2^2\ge0.
\]
A strictly negative upper bound, after allowing every compatible approximation error, would exclude that threshold candidate. The outstanding task is to obtain that negative bound for the **actual prescribed arithmetic coefficients**. [Threshold reduction](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/newman_collisions/notes/12_THRESHOLD_COLLISION_JETS_AND_PAID_LAGUERRE_TEST_20261009.md:148)

The latest progress has three substantial parts:

- **Note 19 describes the correlated errors through the fourth derivative exactly within the bounded holomorphic error class.** Fixing the candidate’s value and first derivative determines two Schur parameters; maximizing over two more leaves a single real parameter. This makes the sharp conditional threshold test much more tractable. The underlying parametrization uses the classical [Schur algorithm](https://arxiv.org/html/1902.02000#S2).
- **The improvement can change a certificate’s conclusion.** An illustrative finite-derivative control has a strictly negative correlated upper bound, while independent error intervals admit a positive value. However, those derivative values have not been established for the prescribed heat coefficients. A second, ordinary-double control gives a positive threshold expression while satisfying every correlated error constraint. Thus error geometry alone cannot supply the missing arithmetic sign. [Note 19](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/newman_collisions/notes/19_HIGHER_SCHUR_PAYMENTS_AND_MULTI_CUTOFF_SIGNED_CONTINUATION_20261010.md:132)
- **Project 09 sharpens the one-sided dual error allowance.** It replaces an absolute penalty by the exact adverse signed penalty on the correlated candidate body. This reduces losses, sometimes substantially, but the same dual coefficients must also support the signed arithmetic estimate. Its Gaussian covariance hierarchy preserves the prescribed weight structure; the covariance contraction still lacks a sign, and the proposed absolute recombination allowance grows exponentially. [Project 09 continuation](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/newman_collisions/09_prime_phase_torus/notes/5_SHARP_ONE_SIDED_DUAL_PAYMENTS_ON_CORRELATED_CANDIDATES_20261010.md:240)

Project 13 now certifies four complete local windows. Each has exact domain
\[
[(2\log M)^{-1},\,1/20]\times[4\pi M^2,\,4\pi M^2+8].
\]

| Cutoff \(M\) | Simple heat zeros at every allowed time | Lower bound for \(\|(Q_t,Q_t'/L)\|\) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 22066 | 13 | \(>0.03728\) |
| 22067 | 12 | \(>0.03117\) |
| 22068 | 12 | \(>0.02205\) |
| 22080 | 13 | \(>0.0032919\) |

These are continuous interval certificates, including shared boundaries and all prescribed terms—not sampled observations. They establish 50 simple zero branches across four disconnected windows. Their time intervals lie approximately between \(0.049988\) and \(0.05\). They leave the spatial gaps, remaining cutoff cells, and the approach to zero time uncovered. Moreover, the derivative margins already imply the first-jet Schur exclusions in these windows, so they have yet to demonstrate additional exclusion power from the curved error body. [Original atlas](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/newman_collisions/notes/18_CORRELATED_HOLOMORPHIC_PAYMENTS_AND_CANDIDATE_COVERAGE_20261010.md:295), [additional windows](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/newman_collisions/13_microlocal_phase_space/notes/5_MULTI_CUTOFF_CORRELATED_CANDIDATE_FAMILY_20261010.md)

I would prioritize the next work as follows:

1. **Build the certified threshold optimizer and connect it to actual complete derivatives.** Handle Schur boundary cases, changing quadratic vertices, and uncertainty in every input interval. Compare its result with independent-error bounds on the same cells. A grid or midpoint evaluation would not suffice.
2. **Target cells with small derivative margins.** The \(M=22080\) window’s first band is a useful initial stress test. Then seek cells where simpler tests remain inconclusive. The meaningful milestone is an actual-coefficient certificate whose conclusion improves because correlations were retained.
3. **Make the main theoretical target a prescribed-coefficient signed estimate on a specified shrinking subsector.** Seek either a negative Schur threshold maximum or a dual bound beating its exact one-sided allowance. Preserve the common height, all four arithmetic channels, amplitude drift, complement interference, and physical derivative residuals.
4. **Keep multiplicity and global coverage explicit.** The fourth-derivative test is vacuous at multiplicity at least four. Higher deflated tests—or a separate multiplicity exclusion—remain necessary. Even a uniform shrinking-sector theorem would require complementary parameter coverage before an RH conclusion.

I verified all 38 files against the latest review snapshot and freshly replayed both exact checkers: **50,157 Schur assertions and 10,081 dual-payment assertions**, reproducing their retained records. These support the algebra and controls; the written proofs and imported analytic assumptions still warrant independent mathematical review. I would like to make the next steps more analytical in nature than numerical to maximize the chance of finding a proof instead of numerical improvements. Given this priority, do you still think the priorities you suggested are optimal?

I would change the ordering. With proof discovery as the priority, the optimizer and additional local certificates should support the work, while the main effort goes toward a signed estimate that uses the prescribed arithmetic coefficients. **No—the ordering should change substantially under that priority.** My previous recommendations emphasized the next concrete certificate. For proof discovery, the main effort should address the missing arithmetic structure; better optimizers and more certified rectangles belong in a supporting role.

The strongest starting point remains project 09, combined with the analytical interference work in project 13. I would revise the priorities as follows.

1. **Seek a prescribed-coefficient signed inequality at an all-real threshold.**

   This is a narrower target than excluding every positive-time collision, and it lets us use the deflated real-root inequality. The essential question is what the genuine weights and common height force that arbitrary positive coefficients or admissible moment vectors do not.

   A concrete first investigation is an analytical summation transformation for one macroscopic block, such as \(\nu N<n\le N\), **together with its interaction with the remaining sum**. Retain the quadratic logarithmic weights, physical derivative multipliers, and all ratio/product channels. The desired intermediate result is a useful one-sided bound after complete recombination, with a uniform remainder on a fixed \(\kappa\)-interval.

   Merely regrouping the existing pair identity would not count as progress. The transformation must expose cancellation or a sign that the present bounds lose. This develops the analytical task already proposed in [Note 13](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/newman_collisions/notes/13_RECENT_HEAT_RESULTS_AND_PATHS_FORWARD_20261009.md:335).

2. **Use Schur geometry to derive transparent analytical sufficient conditions.**

   I would replace “build the numerical optimizer first” with a short supporting task: eliminate the Schur parameters analytically for useful classes of signed derivatives, producing explicit inequalities and margins.

   For example, the algebra in Note 19 gives, in the idealized case
   \[
   f_0=f_1=f_3=0,\qquad
   A=\frac{f_2}{\eta L^2}>2,\qquad
   C=\frac{f_4}{\eta L^4}>24,\qquad \gamma\ge0,
   \]
   the bound
   \[
   U_{\rm Schur}\le
   -3(A-2)(C-24)\eta^2L^6<0.
   \]
   Extending this to explicit tolerances for nonzero lower derivatives, \(f_3\), and signed \(\gamma\) would give a usable analytical target.

   **The substantive theorem would then be proving that the actual arithmetic derivatives satisfy such conditions.** This example should guide the search without restricting it prematurely to one derivative shape. [Note 19’s underlying calculation](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/newman_collisions/notes/19_HIGHER_SCHUR_PAYMENTS_AND_MULTI_CUTOFF_SIGNED_CONTINUATION_20261010.md:200)

3. **Develop multiplicity and parameter coverage alongside the signed argument.**

   Establish which derivative hierarchy the proposed mechanism can handle, especially multiplicity four and above, where the present fourth-derivative test becomes vacuous. Also state precisely which complementary time/height regimes would remain after a shrinking-sector theorem.

   This keeps the analytical objective connected to an eventual proof and can reveal early whether a promising local inequality leaves an unavoidable gap.

I would keep the Gaussian covariance route secondary until there is a new identity controlling its **signed contraction**. Covariance positivity does not supply that sign, and its current absolute allowance grows exponentially. Likewise, further optimization over enlarged moment classes has already encountered positive directions even with zero approximation errors. Those findings justify redirecting effort toward the prescribed coefficients. [Project 09’s limitations](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/newman_collisions/09_prime_phase_torus/notes/5_SHARP_ONE_SIDED_DUAL_PAYMENTS_ON_CORRELATED_CANDIDATES_20261010.md:240)

My recommended next milestone is therefore **a uniform analytical lemma about complete signed recombination**, even on a limited subsector. Numerical work would serve to challenge conjectured lemmas or verify identities, rather than determine the research milestones.

The audits also confirm where the proof still needs new input: the remaining signed correlations and higher multiplicities. Zero density adds a positive multiple of \((\log x)q_2^2\) to the necessary threshold bound, strengthening the exclusion test without changing the holomorphic approximation error. I’ve also established a general-multiplicity version of the central Schur cone, under an explicit lower-jet hypothesis. Whether the actual arithmetic sums satisfy either cone remains open.

The cross-checks found no mathematical correction to the new formulas. I continued analytically and saved three notes with full derivations.

- [Note 20: analytical Schur cones](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/newman_collisions/notes/20_ANALYTIC_SCHUR_CONES_AND_DENSITY_STRENGTHENED_THRESHOLDS_20261010.md) gives explicit sufficient exclusion inequalities without optimizing over Schur parameters.   \[
  2q_3^2-3q_2q_4-
  \left(\gamma+\frac{9\log x}{2D_0^2}\right)q_2^2\ge0,
  \]
  where \(D_0\) depends on the imported, symbolic counting constant.

- [Project 09 Note 6: prescribed-coefficient smoothing](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/newman_collisions/09_prime_phase_torus/notes/6_ANALYTIC_COMMON_FACTOR_SMOOTHING_AND_PRIMITIVE_SIGNED_FRONTIER_20261010.md) transforms the large-common-factor ratio coefficients into explicit integrals and endpoint corrections, with a uniformly vanishing global remainder. Three advances emerged:

- **Exact diagonal cancellation.** A correction controlled by the genuine candidate constraints makes all four pair kernels vanish on the diagonal. A narrow macroscopic near-diagonal band then has a rigorously vanishing payment.
- **Controlled oscillatory transformations.** Product and primitive sums now have analytical representations with globally bounded, vanishing remainders. They retain both signed channels, literal cutoffs, mixed terms, and boundary contributions.
- **A precise limitation of reflection.** The prescribed leading stationary reflection preserves the threshold quadratic and changes the cutoff range. It cannot supply the required negative sign by itself.

The next proof target is therefore a **candidate-conditioned upper bound for the coupled resonant integrals and boundary terms**, strong enough to beat all retained payments. The opposite threshold sign remains open.
